Prevention: Crop rotation with crops other than sorghum and pearl millet.
Rotating with legumes improves soil nutrients and maize plants’ ability to tolerate stalk borers
Plant stress tolerant varieties such as
ST Plant early in rainy periods
Short rains: early to mid-September; Long rains: early to mid-November
Desmodium in between maize rows to repel stalk borers from the maize.
Plant napier grass along the borders of the maize as a trap crop to pull stalk borers away from the maize.
Tagetes spp. ) to attract natural enemies
After harvest, destroy crop residues(e.g. old stalks) in order to kill larvae and pupae in stalks
Monitoring: Three weeks after planting, begin inspecting maize plants two times per week.
Observe plants for holes in leaves and dead hearts
Consider carrying out early controls when 3 – 10% of young plants in population are damaged
In the later stages of the infestation, larvae bore into upper maize stalks and dead-heart symptoms appear.
At this stage, control measures are too late because larvae are protected inside the stalks
Direct Control: Early control of young larvae that have not yet entered stalks:
Put one bottle cap of ash dust into leaf-funnel of young plant; Apply
Neem seed cake powder 25 – 50g/L water onto young plants every 10 days until flowering; Apply hot pepper solution onto young plants every 10 days until flowering
Place egg cards with the parasitic wasp
Pyrethroid with contact and residual activity
